g.text: Build GPT-2 from tensors up. Tokens, embeddings, LayerNorm, Attention, MLP, Unembed, Sampling.
Every component reads from it and writes back. Attention moves info between positions.
MLP does per-position computation. LayerNorm normalizes before each component.
GPT-2 is PRE-NORM: LN is applied to the
INPUT of each block, then added to the
(LN after the +). Pre-norm is easier to
train deep because residual stays clean.
Rescale to zero mean, unit variance across d_model dim, then apply learned scale/shift.
For each (batch, position), operating on the d_model vector x:
var = x.var(dim=-1, keepdim=True, unbiased=False) ← divide by N
y = x_hat * gamma + beta ← per-feature learned scale/shift
PyTorch's default t.var(unbiased=True) divides by N-1 (Bessel's correction).
Also: sqrt(var + eps) is NOT the same as (std + eps). Get this wrong
and per-layer accuracy is off by ~1%. The most common bug in this exercise.
Q, K, V projections. Scaled dot-product with causal mask. Multi-head parallelism.
For each layer, given x ∈ (B, S, d_model):
q = x @ W_Q ∈ (B, S, n_heads, d_head) ← per-head projections
k = x @ W_K ∈ (B, S, n_heads, d_head)
v = x @ W_V ∈ (B, S, n_heads, d_head)
scores = einsum('bqhd, bkhd -> bhqk', q, k) / sqrt(d_head) ← QK^T scaled
mask = torch.tril(ones(S, S)) ← lower triangular, causal
pattern = softmax(scores, dim=-1) ∈ (B, H, S_query, S_key)
z = einsum('bhqk, bkhd -> bqhd', pattern, v) ← weighted sum
attn_out = einsum('bqhd, hdm -> bqm', z, W_O) ← recombine heads
Dot product of two random d_head-dim vectors has variance ~ d_head.
Without scaling: softmax gets peakier as d_head grows, gradients vanish.
sqrt(d_head) normalization keeps score variance ~ 1 regardless of head dim.
Set future positions to -inf BEFORE softmax → they become exactly 0 after.
Setting to -inf AFTER softmax + renormalizing sort-of works but leaks
probability mass onto them briefly, then re-normalizes. Numerically less clean.
torch pattern: scores.masked_fill_(~mask, IGNORE) where IGNORE = -1e5 (or -inf).
Two linear layers with GELU nonlinearity in between. d_mlp = 4x d_model.
h = gelu( x @ W_in + b_in ) ∈ (B, S, d_mlp = 4 * d_model)
y = h @ W_out + b_out ∈ (B, S, d_model)
PER-POSITION: applied independently at each seq index.
NO cross-position information flow. That's attention's job.
Bigger d_mlp = more capacity for the
MLP's key-value memory, but more compute.
MLP has ~2/3 of all model params.
